title_original: Java4Shell: RCE, one application at a time
description: On 17 November 2026, Oracle and the OpenJDK project shipped fixes for CVE-2026-114938, a memory corruption bug in the Base64 decoder built into the Java runtime. Calif, who found it and named it Java4Shell, reports unauthenticated RCE against Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate in their default configurations. Calif scores it 9.2 on CVSS v4.0. Oracle scores it 8.1 on v3.1, with attack complexity high.The postJava4Shell: RCE, one application at a timeappeared first onPentera.

title_original: Cato CTRL Threat Brief on How Java4Shell Turns Base64 Decoding Into an Enterprise Risk
description: Executive summary Java4Shell (CVE-2026-114938), disclosed on 17 November 2026, is a memory-corruption flaw in Java’s accelerated Base64 decoder. Malformed input can crash an affected JVM, and external researchers have demonstrated application-specific remote code execution. Exposure requires an affected JVM on an x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI and BW support, with the vulnerable decoding path enabled...The postCato CTRL Threat Brief on How Java4Shell Turns Base64 Decoding Into an Enterprise Riskappeared first onCato Networks.

title_original: Cato CTRL Threat Brief and Insights on OPTIMJACK

title_original: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in NGINX: CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007
description: Two critical HTTP/2 flaws can allow attackers to compromise NGINX servers, putting the websites, APIs, and sensitive data they handle at risk.
